newsitem.title: QATAR: Rasgas sees end to minimum price on LNG sales.
newsitem.headline: Rasgas sees end to minimum price on LNG sales.

text.p: Exporters of liquefied natural gas (LNG) are unlikely in the future to be able to guarantee minimum sale prices in their long-term supply contracts, the head of a Qatari LNG firm said on Tuesday.

"The market is changing. There is no question about it. It was started by Oman LNG," Neil Kelley, managing director of the Ras Laffan Liquefied Natural Gas Company (Rasgas) said on the sidelines of a gas conference in Qatar.
Rasgas last month dropped its floor-price provision in exchange for its customer Korea Gas Corp (KOGAS) agreeing to double its liftings of Rasgas LNG to 4.8 million tonnes a year.
First-phase exports to KOGAS will start in 1999.

KOGAS last year negotiated a deal with the rival Oman LNG Company that had no minimum price requirement. LNG producers have argued they need minimum pricing to ensure returns on the $5-billion-plus capital cost of a typical LNG plant.

State-owned Qatar General Petroleum Corp has 63 percent stake in Rasgas with U.S. Mobil Corp 25 percent, Japan's Itochu 3.5 percent, Nissho Iwai 3.5 percent and an undeclared South Korean entity five percent.
